description: FORCE_DISABLE_SHM: keep DES S-boxes in constant mem, drop per-block shared copy+SYNC prologue. ncu: comp is ADU-bound 96% (divergent const->shared copy), NOT DES — (d>>16)!=s2 filter rejects ~65535/65536 so DES/512 LDS ~never run in bench. 944.2/941.0 vs 931.5 = +1.2-1.4%, within ~1-2% noise band; consistent but sub-threshold. selftest PASS.

Fold hex-decode into _comp (read pws[gid] directly, precedent m32700/m22700/m70100) and empty _init, dropping the per-candidate tmps round-trip (init 4-word store + comp 4-word reload) on this memory-bound pipeline; also decode d first and apply the existing (d>>16)!=s2 2-byte reject BEFORE decoding a/b/c, so the ~65535/65536 rejected candidates read only 2 words + partial decode instead of full init+decode+store+reload. ncu: init was mem-bound (41% mem/11% compute), comp SM-bound on SHM copy but filter rejects all (benchmark fixed tail => d constant, prior FORCE_DISABLE_SHM only +1.2%). 931.5 -> 1114.0 = +19.6%, selftest PASS.

Filter reject reads only pws.i[7]: (d>>16)==b2|(b3<<8) is decoded entirely from i[7] (i[6] only feeds the discarded low half b0/b1 of d), so compute d_hi from i[7] alone, apply (d_hi!=s2) reject, and load i[6]+decode full a/b/c/d only on the ~1/65536 passing path. Value-identical (d_hi==d>>16), selftest PASS. Cuts the dominant reject path from 2 pws-word loads + 4 hex decodes to 1 load + 2 decodes. Measured 1133.3 then 1115.4 vs best 1114.0 = ~+0.9% avg, within ~1-2% noise band (first run high-side noise). Sub-threshold like the earlier FORCE_DISABLE_SHM +1.2%: i[6] and i[7] share the same 128-byte cache line so dropping one load does not reduce the binding DRAM/L2 traffic; only load-instruction count + 2 ALU decodes drop, not the bottleneck.

Pin comp block size to 512 threads via FIXED_THREAD_COUNT (CUDA __launch_bounds__(512,0), honored: host launches MIN(kernel_wgs4=512, kernel_threads>=992)=512). Motivation: ncu on current best shows comp DRAM-bound (71.9% mem / 31% compute, achieved occ 55.3%) with theoretical occ hard-capped at 64.58% because the default 992-thread block = 31 warps fits only 1 block/SM (warp cap, not just regs/shared); 512 threads = 16 warps should fit ~3 blocks/SM = 48 warps = 100% occ (40 regs, 12KB shared) to hide DRAM latency on the strided pws[gid] reject read. Measured 1072.1 vs 1114.0 = -3.8%, selftest PASS (correct, just slower). Smaller blocks TRIPLE the block count, and each block pays the S-box constant->shared copy + SYNC_THREADS prologue, which is a large fraction of the trivial read+decode+reject work; the tripled prologue overhead outweighs the latency-hiding gain. The 992-thread block amortizes the prologue better. Occupancy-via-smaller-blocks lever CLOSED for this kernel (prologue cost scales with block count).

FORCE_DISABLE_SHM + FIXED_THREAD_COUNT(512) on comp, combined. Hypothesis: bec1836a8 (512-only, -3.8%) blamed the tripled constant->shared S-box copy prologue; removing REAL_SHM (0 shared) should let ~100% occupancy from 512-thread blocks (16 warps, 3 blocks/SM = 48 warps vs 992-thread 31-warp/1-block = 64.6% cap) hide DRAM latency on the strided pws[gid] reject read WITHOUT repaying the prologue. Measured 1138.3 then 1128.9 vs best 1114.0 = +2.18%/+1.34% (avg +1.76%), inside the ~1-2% band, not reproducibly beyond 2%. selftest PASS (correct). This is basically the FORCE_DISABLE_SHM-alone +1.2% effect plus a marginal occupancy bump: the kernel is DRAM-BANDWIDTH-bound (71.9% mem at 55% achieved occ), not latency-bound, so more warps in flight do not raise achieved bandwidth enough to clear the band. Occupancy-via-smaller-blocks lever now CLOSED even after removing the prologue that bec blamed.

Combine the two previously-sub-threshold orthogonal instruction-reducers never tested together: FORCE_DISABLE_SHM (drop the per-block S-box constant->shared copy + SYNC_THREADS prologue that ALL threads pay before the (d>>16)!=s2 reject; +1.2% alone, exp2) + read-only-i7 (compute filter word d_hi=b2|b3<<8 from pws[gid].i[7] alone, load i[6]+decode full d/a/b/c only on the ~1/65536 passing path; +0.9% alone, exp4). Both value-identical, selftest PASS. Measured 1119.6 vs best 1114.0 = +0.5%, sub-threshold. The levers do NOT stack additively: both cut instructions/barriers off the reject path but the kernel is DRAM-bound (71.9% mem) on the intrinsic 260B AoS pws[gid] scatter (host-fixed layout), so reducing prologue/decode instructions does not raise the binding effective bandwidth. Reinforces roofline: exp2 +1.2%, exp4 +0.9%, exp6 (noSHM+FIXED512) +1.76%, and now noSHM+i7 +0.5% ALL cluster in-band. .cl-side roofline confirmed for m27000.
